testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Reading a text message while driving is:

options.text: Allowed only if you are not pulling a trailer.

questions.explanation: Sending and reading text messages while driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Only be used when it is wet outside.
Be used to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and oil from air brake system tanks. Always drain the tank completely when operating the drain.

questions.question: Look ahead at the road ____ in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot and react to hazards before you reach them. Watch for vehicles entering the highway or changing into your lane.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery right after it rains because:

options.text: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Tires are not made to drive in wet weather.
The water has not yet washed away dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil and grease on the road surface. This creates a slick film that has not yet washed away.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions need double clutching to shift gears. This technique takes practice to master.

questions.question: Skids happen when:

options.text: Tires lose their grip on the road.
There is too much weight in the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires lose their grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Skids happen when tires lose grip on the road. This can be caused by over-braking, over-accelerating, over-steering, or driving too fast.

questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs are:

options.text: Safe to use if a professional did the repairs.
Safe to use if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are not safe. They must be replaced before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: What is Gross Combination Weight?

options.text: The total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo
The total weight of a single vehicle without its load
The maximum weight allowed by the manufacturer

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Combination Weight is the total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo combined.

questions.question: If a speed limit is posted, the posted speed:

options.text: May be exceeded if passing another vehicle.
May be exceeded if driving in a rural area.

questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed for ideal conditions. You must slow down as road conditions require. Never exceed the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Improperly loaded cargo can:

options.text: Hurt or kill the driver during a sudden stop.
Make it easier to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hurt or kill the driver during a sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Improperly secured or loaded cargo is dangerous. Loose cargo can fall during a sudden stop and injure or kill the driver.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Jump quickly from low to high.

questions.explanation: Check your vehicle's gauges before you drive. After you start the engine, the coolant temperature should slowly rise to the normal operating level.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, you should:
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you realize you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation. Keep driving at a safe speed.

questions.question: If your driver's license is suspended:

options.text: You do not have to tell anyone.
It will not affect your CDL.

questions.explanation: If you are convicted of any traffic violation while driving any vehicle, you must tell your employer within 30 days. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: A jogger wearing headphones:

options.text: Is probably aware of their surroundings.
May not be aware of their surroundings.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of their surroundings.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear your vehicle coming and could do something unsafe because they do not know you are there.

questions.question: Looking ahead at the road:

options.text: Gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard.
Is not recommended because it distracts you.
Is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard.
questions.explanation: Always watch for hazards ahead on the road. This gives you time to react before you reach the hazard.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before every trip. Make sure they are positioned correctly.

questions.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Can cause a vehicle to tip over.
Should be used in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause a vehicle to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over than cargo with a low center of gravity. Always place cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: As you go down and speed up

questions.explanation: Slow down and shift to a lower gear before you go down a hill. If you do not start slowly enough, your brakes may overheat and fail.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must check all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, you will check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: In a leaf spring:
questions.explanation: Check that leaf springs do not have missing or broken leaves. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must be taken out of service until it is fixed.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only after you apply the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Use wheel chocks when parking on a flat surface. This is very important if your vehicle does not have spring brakes. Wheel chocks prevent the trailer from rolling.

questions.question: If there is a worker in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit.
Drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower than the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Follow the posted speed limit in work zones. When workers are present, drive even slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal all the way down and release. If it does not return to normal, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal all the way down and release. If the brake squeaks, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic brakes by pumping the pedal three times. Then press the pedal down hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or another problem with the brakes.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: Press it down quickly with both feet.

questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly. This helps your vehicle stop safely and smoothly.

questions.question: Drivers stuck behind a slow vehicle often:
questions.explanation: Drivers often tailgate slow-moving vehicles. If someone is tailgating you, let them pass safely.

questions.question: Poor weight balance:
questions.explanation: Unbalanced cargo makes a vehicle harder to control. Always distribute cargo weight evenly.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should weight be placed?

options.text: As far to the left as possible.

questions.explanation: Heavy cargo placed high makes the vehicle more likely to tip. Place cargo as low as possible to prevent tipping.

questions.question: When going down a hill, how can you use less braking?
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, slow down and shift to a lower gear. This lets the engine help slow the vehicle. Using brakes too much on a hill can cause them to overheat and fail.

questions.question: A driver with a window open in cold weather may be:
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of impaired driving. A driver with the window down in cold weather may be impaired. Impaired drivers create danger for everyone.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, they are safe on the rear wheels.
Yes, they are safe when carrying heavy loads.

questions.explanation: Never use wheels or rims that have been welded. They are not safe.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, they are safe to use on the rear tires.
Yes, they are safe if you are carrying a light load.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are never safe to use.

questions.question: Is eating while driving safe?

options.text: Yes, if the food is easy to eat.

questions.explanation: Eating, smoking, or drinking while driving are distracting and dangerous. Plan ahead and take breaks to eat on long trips.

questions.question: What should you do with items on a flatbed?

options.text: They do not need to be strapped down because they are heavy.
They do not need to be strapped down if you drive slower than 35 mph.

questions.explanation: All cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to prevent it from shifting or falling off during transport.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles driving behind a truck?

options.text: They may not be able to see objects in front of the truck.
They usually have a clear view of the road ahead.
They do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be able to see objects in front of the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks block the view of drivers behind them. Flash your brake lights and warn other drivers before you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning happen?

options.text: It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. You do not need much water for this to happen. Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: What should you do with your mirrors when making a tight turn?

options.text: Do not use them because they are distracting.
Use them, but not very often.

questions.explanation: Always be aware of your surroundings. Check your mirrors regularly, especially when merging, changing lanes, turning, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: What task might be on a CDL vehicle inspection test?
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you may need to check the engine oil level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: What must you have to transport hazardous materials that require placards?

options.text: Permission to transport only at night.

questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to operate any vehicle that transports hazardous materials requiring placards.

questions.question: How should you brake in a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the brakes several times before holding the brake pedal down.
Press the brake pedal as hard as possible every time.

questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in one without ABS. ABS automatically prevents wheel lockup when you apply the brakes.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: They hold enough air for one brake application only.
They hold enough air for several brake applications if the compressor fails.
They only hold air during emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold enough air for several brake applications if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: When making tight turns or maneuvers, a driver should:

options.text: Open their door for a better view.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks usually have:

options.text: Special permission to cross railroad tracks.

questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity. Be careful when driving with them because the cargo can shift during transit.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
Only use turn signals if another vehicle is next to them.
Not use a turn signal if the lane change is obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, you should:

options.text: Place as little weight as possible over the axles.
Balance the weight evenly over the axles.
Place weight only directly over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Balance the weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Balance your cargo properly. Too much weight on one axle damages it and makes steering harder. Too little weight on an axle reduces grip and makes handling difficult.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, you should NOT:

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.

questions.explanation: If your engine catches fire, turn off the engine immediately. Do not open the hood if you can avoid it.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic flow, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow it).

questions.question: If you don't know the area where you need to back up, you should:

options.text: Get out and walk around to see the area first.
Not use both side mirrors because it is distracting.
Wait for someone else to back up first so you can see how they do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around to see the area first.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out of your vehicle and check your path. Look for obstacles on the sides and overhead.

questions.question: Within 10 minutes of stopping on the side of the road, you must:
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes.

questions.question: A trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: The trailer brake hand valve prevents the truck from rolling back when you start moving from a stop.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Move quickly to stay out of other drivers' ways.

questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Ask someone to help watch your blind spots whenever you can.
